title: Minimax Estimation of the Fraction Benefiting with Opposite-Treatment Replay Queries

proof_attempt_summary: Attempted sharp proportional-budget precision profiles and their sequential-versus-batch comparison for fixed individual benefit under stable replays. Delivered a lossless original-record two-urn reduction, certified finite minimax programs, five exact small-case feedback equalities, and a regular-interior batch upper transfer; policy-uniform adaptive posterior lower bounds, boundary gluing, and certified general-budget controls remain open. Math review passed, but the normalized achieved tier was incremental against field, so the operator-directed result is downgraded; formalization was not started.
tldr: The causal target is the fraction of fixed labelled units individually improved by a binary treatment. Under the maintained stable opposite-treatment observation channel, the complete original-record minimax problem reduces exactly to two controlled finite urns, retaining both the beneficiary and nuisance strata. For every finite public size and exact replay budget, we give attained minimax strategies and least-favourable count priors, explicit convex semialgebraic programs, and a terminating rational certificate procedure that exports original assignment, replay and clipped decision laws. Exact rational certificates prove that the sequential and factual-conditioned batch values agree at \((4,2),(5,2),(5,3),(6,2),(6,3)\). Evaluated proportional-budget profiles and their complete feedback atlas remain open; these finite equalities and the interior diagnostic do not resolve them.
gap: Sudijono--Dobriban--Tchetgen Tchetgen, Theorem 2.2, solves unrestricted-design binary SATE estimation without opposite queries. He, Theorem 2.1, solves hypergeometric domain totals with a known ancillary sample-size law. Neither result evaluates the fixed beneficiary target when the factual partition is informative and replay answers control subsequent sampling.
fill: The exact ordered two-urn likelihood connects original designs to controlled finite-population information. The required result evaluates both proportional risk profiles, proves total observable attainment and all-policy lower bounds, resolves the feedback difference, and gives arbitrary-tolerance original finite certificates. The kernel is chosen-design minimax precision; a fixed-design central limit theorem is supporting methodology only.
